findings.title: The DAO hack
findings.description: The split path paid ether out through an external call before the caller's balance was zeroed, so the attacker re-entered the split function from inside the payout and withdrew repeatedly in one transaction.

findings.title: call.value() with all remaining gas in payOut()
findings.description: A low-level call.value() forwards all remaining gas to the recipient, which can run code and call back in before this function finishes.

findings.title: Unchecked send() in executeProposal()
findings.description: send() forwards only 2,300 gas and returns false on failure; the result is ignored, so a failed payment passes silently.

incident.name: The DAO hack
incident.loss_note: Wikipedia: about 3.6 million ether moved out, roughly a third of the 11.5 million committed, valued at around $50 million at the time. Atzei et al. (eprint 2016/1007) instead say about $60M came under the attacker's control.
incident.cause: The split path paid ether out through an external call before the caller's balance was zeroed, so the attacker re-entered the split function from inside the payout and withdrew repeatedly in one transaction.
incident.summary: On 17 June 2016 an attacker drained ether from The DAO by calling the split function recursively before balances were updated. The ether went into a child DAO that had a 28-day holding period, and the Ethereum Foundation blog proposed a soft fork aimed at that child DAO's code. The funds were later recovered through the hard fork.
